source.title: Reasoning-to-Defend: Safety-Aware Reasoning Can Defend Large Language Models from Jailbreaking
source.authors: Junda Zhu; Lingyong Yan; Shuai-Qiang Wang; Da-Wei Yin; Lei Sha

record.tranche_reason: The study trains models to assess safety at each reasoning step using pivot tokens, then measures harmful-response rates under jailbreak attacks. This is a different training method from the claim’s original fine-tuning recipes, but its results bear on whether stepwise safety training improves robustness.
record.gate_note: The study reports ASRs for R2D-trained models and ablations under jailbreak attacks. It does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, isolate ordinary benign fine-tuning, or directly test compliant-prefill or decoding-change bypasses. The attack results below are included as outcomes of the trained safety method, not as evidence for a particular bypass mechanism.
record.test_reason: R2D is a jailbreak defense (stepwise safety pivot tokens distilled into reasoning traces) evaluated only by its own ASR against prompt-level attacks (PAIR, GCG, JBC, AutoDAN, ZeroShot, FewShot) and other defenses. It never measures safety depth: there are no prefilling or decoding attacks, no per-position KL, no harmful or benign fine-tuning attacks, and no check that safety now extends past the first tokens. Qi et al. is cited only in passing, saying hard refusal generalizes poorly. Lower jailbreak ASR from a new defense does not show whether deepening safety beyond the opening tokens fixes shallow alignment, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct: R2D (SwaRD distillation plus CPO pivot tokens) gives lower jailbreak ASR than prior defenses, without over-refusal or capability loss, and ablations show both components help. The authors do not frame this as deepening safety alignment beyond the first tokens.
record.recipe_differences: R2D uses LoRA training on reasoning trajectories and stepwise safety pivot tokens, synthesized from 52k Alpaca samples and 520 AdvBench samples; it is not harmful-only fine-tuning or ordinary benign instruction fine-tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR varies across model and attack. The study also compares R2D with R2D-n, which concludes reasoning during inference, and reports ablation effects for removing pivot tokens or CPO. Over-refusal evaluations use two judges, Qwenv2.5-72B and Dic-Judge.

fits_no_version.finding: Stepwise safety pivot tokens trained into reasoning cut prompt-level jailbreak ASR. Examples: Qwen2-7B JBC 92% to 0%; Vicuna-7B JBC only 92% to 37%. General benchmarks are kept, and removing pivot tokens raises ASR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-aware stepwise reasoning training reduces prompt-level jailbreak success (a defense-efficacy claim, not a depth claim).

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, 2025
record.problems: ASR is judged by benchmark guardrail/discriminator models; no ASR uncertainty estimates are reported. The study does not isolate the contribution of the benign versus harmful portions of the training data. Some ASRs remain substantial after R2D, and ablation outcomes are not uniformly improved by pivot tokens.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached. Omitted the remaining Table 4 w/o CPO attack/model ablation rows, as well as the HarmBench Figure 3 per-model attack comparisons and Table 5 defense comparisons. Table 4 is in the ablation section; the HarmBench results are in Figure 3 and Table 5. The omitted Table 4 rows compare additional ablations of the study’s method; the figure values are plotted rather than transcribed as a complete numeric table.

untested.parts: No benign fine-tuning attack on safety.
No per-token KL or positional analysis.
No prefilling or decoding-change attacks. GCG and JBC are used only as transferred prompt attacks to score the defense.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.
R2D adds stepwise safety tokens, but the study never tests depth: no prefill robustness, no per-position analysis, no robustness to further fine-tuning.

record.verdict_notes: The reader labelled this as testing V7. It does not: the measure is the study's own defense performance against prompt jailbreaks, with no check of depth. Table 4 covers 7 models (no Vicuna-13B), so the t4-vic13 rows are fabricated. The t4-llama pivot rows marked 'reversed' are 1-point ablation differences. The training data includes 520 AdvBench refusals, so the trained safety behaviour is supervised by design.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-only fine-tuning intended to induce compliance is tested.
The study does not isolate ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning; training combines Alpaca and safety-aware reasoning trajectories from AdvBench.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
The paper evaluates jailbreak attacks generally but does not isolate compliant prefilling, suffix bypass, or decoding changes as mechanisms.
No localization of safety to a small set of weights or ranks is tested.
The study does not test why safety would be shallow or whether data or objective causes shallowness.

The study trains stepwise safety pivot tokens and evaluates jailbreak ASR, but does not measure whether safety behavior is distributed across response positions or test persistence under other training or inference conditions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: R2D-trained non-reasoning and reasoning models under the reported JailbreakBench attacks
reader_labels.reason: R2D lowers ASR across most reported model/attack combinations, often markedly; the comparisons are in rows t1-llama-pair through t2-qwqn-jbc.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Models and attack settings with residual or comparatively high ASR after R2D, including Vicunav1.5-7B on JBC and R17B on PAIR
reader_labels.reason: The improvement is incomplete in some settings: ASR remains 37% and 24%, respectively, and R2D-n also leaves sizable ASRs in several conditions; see the cited rows.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Removing pivot tokens usually increases ASR relative to R2D, with particularly large increases for several model/attack combinations; the no-pivot and full-R2D comparisons are in rows t4-llama-jbc-pivot through t4-qwq-jbc-pivot.
